name: LiXR
author: 100demons
summary: A fixed-point drum voice with feedback FM, a pitch envelope and a sample-rate decimator where the filter would be.

knobs.does: waveform: sine on the left, triangle in the centre, saw then rectangle on the right. Past 0.65 it adds noise, and past 0.85 a clap-like burst; SHAPE reduces the noise
feedback FM, from none to a quarter cycle of modulation, on a square law; the top of the range is the wild part
pitch envelope: depth (0 to 48 semitones) and decay time together
labelled **Rate**: the decimator's sample rate, clean at 0 to a coarse, aliased buzz at 127

cpu_note: 6,335 to 6,499 instructions per block and per voice in the OS's own voice loop, against 6,572 for TONE (measured in emulation; not measured on the machine). It has no load governor of its own, so several LiXR tracks at once can starve the processor.
emulator_proof: model27 tools/emu/test_lixr.py in the real OS voice loop (Unicorn): sound through the stock amp chain, no unmapped access, stock KICK unchanged

credits.what: the engine code, tables and design
the LXR drum voice as a specification and a listening reference; no code, table or sample copied
